settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The download is gated by an explicit authorization check (PermissionFactory.getPagePermission(att, "view") + authmgr.checkPermission, lines 241-247), so only users allowed to view the attachment reach the header-write.
Many servlet containers reject CR/LF characters in header values, which would neutralize response splitting even if the name carried them.

The 304 branch (line 253) uses att.getName() and HttpUtil.checkFor304, showing attachment names are used elsewhere in a benign comparison only; no evidence was read that the name can contain control characters.
missing_evidence: Implementation of the upload path (AttachmentManager.saveAttachment and BasicAttachmentProvider) that would show whether attachment names are validated/sanitized before storage.
Definition of Attachment.getFileName()/getName() to determine whether the name is normalized or filtered.
Container-level behavior for addHeader with CR/LF, which was not observable from the repository source.
preconditions: An attachment is uploaded and persisted under a name containing CR, LF, or a double-quote character (or such a name can otherwise be stored in the attachment provider).
A user with view permission on that attachment requests the download endpoint, causing doGet to reach line 269-270.
The target servlet container does not itself reject/strip CR/LF in addHeader values.
candidates.title: Attachment download echoes stored filename into Content-Disposition header without sanitization (HTTP header injection)

counter_evidence: The redirect target is not used raw: it is wrapped in validateNextPage(nextPage, <engine ERROR URL>), indicating an existing validation/fallback mechanism that was likely added specifically to prevent arbitrary redirects.
The redirect only fires after a successful attachment fetch and permission check, which limits who can trigger it.
No code path was read in which nextpage bypasses validateNextPage, so the weakness is conditional on the helper's internals.
missing_evidence: The implementation/body of validateNextPage (not present in the readable spans).
Whether sendRedirect receives a normalized/encoded value or the raw parameter.
Any configured property controlling allowed redirect hosts.
preconditions: A logged-in or anonymous user can reach AttachmentServlet.doGet for an attachment they may view (the redirect at line 303-305 executes after the attachment is streamed successfully).
validateNextPage does not fully restrict the destination to same-origin relative URLs.
An attacker can induce a victim to request the attachment URL with a crafted nextpage value.
candidates.title: Attachment download 'nextpage' parameter is redirected via an unread validation helper (open redirect candidate)

counter_evidence: The value is used only in log/diagnostic context strings in the read span; no HTML/JSP output sink for it was observed.
Fire/event handling on line 108 uses a separately computed page name, not this string.
WatchDog and log4j behavior were not read, so no output sink is demonstrated.
missing_evidence: WikiServletFilter and WatchDog implementations, to see whether the state string is ever rendered to a response.
Whether JSP templates or admin pages display NDC/watchdog contents.
preconditions: A logging or diagnostic consumer renders the NDC/watchdog state without encoding.
An attacker can send a request whose URI contains the injection payload.
candidates.title: WikiJSPFilter uses the request URI directly in log/NDC context and WatchDog state
